newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Galleon gas project approved-Shell Expro.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Galleon gas project approved-Shell Expro.

text.p: The 135 million stg second phase development of the Galleon natural gas field in the southern North Sea was approved by Britain's Department of Trade and Industry, operator Shell UK Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) said on Thursday.

Shell Expro said the project will include the installation of a wellhead platform and the drilling of 11 development wells to drain the northwestern area of the field which straddles Blocks 48/14, 48/15a, 48/19a and 48/20a,

"This approval marks a major step in the development of Galleon and clearly demonstrates our intention to secure gas supplies from the field well into the next century," said Gary Vassie, Shell Expro gas director.

Installation of the platform is planned for the end of 1997 and first gas from the initial three development wells is due on stream in October 1998. It is expected to recover at least 7870 billion standard cubic feet of gas, Shell Expro said.
Gas will be exported to shore via the Sole Pit Offshore Transportation System (SPOTS) landing at the Shell Expro reception terminal at Bacton on the Norfolk, east England coast.
The majority of the gas is contracted to British Gas until 2010, with the balance available for sale to other companies.
Shell Expro, which is a joint venture of Shell and Exxon Corp, has an 80 percent stake in the field while Conoco (UK) Ltd and PowerGen (North Sea) Ltd each hold 10 percent stakes.
